S1.rationale: The core Python task runner executes selected list/read/write/run_python tools, returns results to an OpenAI-compatible model and rejects premature done under configured checks. No concrete task failure is evidenced beyond its intended experimental controls.

S2.rationale: One task at a time has sequential tool dispatch; strategy comparisons across task runs are separate experiments, not interacting viable S1 units. Deferring done until other tool calls complete does not create inter-agent regulation.

S3.rationale: Step, no-tool, and rejection budgets bound a single coding run, and the verifier vetoes its completion. There is no operational portfolio with a separate current authority requiring a supported scheduling/resource change.

S3*.rationale: DefaultFailVerifier can examine work products and tool logs independently of a done message but is a local task acceptance gate, not an independent audit of managerial reports. No false-result incident motivates a new S3-star channel in this research harness.

S4.rationale: ContextManager tests full/compact/compact_clear fixed strategies and experiment scripts generate comparative reports, but an external human chooses policy; no accepted autonomous future capability mutation is present or natively demanded.

S5.rationale: Experiment authors predefine task constraints, evidence checklist and workspace side-effect rules. Fixed task policy is not a legitimate ultimate-identity change decision, and the assessment provides no product need to grant one.
